rationale: The student mistakenly added the denominators (getting tenths instead of fifths), failing to recognize that the denominator defines the unit size which remains constant during addition. Switching from a fraction bar to interactive circular slices in fraction-circles lets the student physically combine pieces into a single whole circle and observe directly that joining fifths results in more fifths, not tenths.
intent: Focus on visual fraction addition and building fractions with common denominators like fourths, sixths, or eighths (avoid fifths to prevent giving away the active challenge 2/5 + 1/5). Provide challenges where the student builds and compares shaded slices in a circle to directly visualize that adding parts leaves the denominator unchanged.

data.description: Practise building visual fractions using circles with denominators from the fraction pool to understand addition concepts.

judgement.reasoning: The student obstacle is adding the denominators (e.g., answering 3/10 for 2/5 + 1/5). The generated content merely asks the student to shade static individual fractions on a circle (e.g., shade 1/4, shade 2/3). It does not present any addition context, combining parts, or visual addition steps to demonstrate that the size/number of total pieces remains unchanged during addition.
judgement.verdict: No teacher would use this detour right now because it only has students shade single fractions rather than addressing or illustrating fraction addition.
